title: X Feed Digest
summary: Enterprise AI discussion in this batch was much more about control surfaces than raw model launches: Anthropic moving Claude Platform into customer AWS accounts, Feishu/Lark emerging as an agent workspace, and operators asking for better ways to supervise multiple concurrent agent runs.

The most practical developer signal came from workflow glue rather than new foundation models — token-trimming wrappers, parallel Codex windows, and HTML+JSON system maps all point to the same idea: harness quality is still the biggest force multiplier.

Markets/news conversation centered on AI's financial plumbing instead of hype-cycle narratives, especially legal interpretation around Anthropic secondary shares and the shift toward customized models as the real engine of inference economics.
The clearest hard-news item was security: the TanStack npm compromise was a sharp reminder that modern supply-chain attacks can abuse trusted release provenance, not just sloppy package hygiene.

items.title: @berryxia: Claude Platform Moves Inside AWS Accounts
items.body: Anthropic can now run Managed Agents, prompt caching, and built-in tools inside a customer's own AWS account, keeping billing, IAM, and security review in AWS. The significance is less the feature list than the distribution shift: it removes one of the biggest enterprise blockers to deploying agent systems at scale.

items.title: @wsl8297: RTK Cuts Coding-Agent Log Bloat
items.body: RTK sits between coding agents and noisy shell output, deduplicating and compressing logs before they hit context. If the reported 60%–90% token savings holds up, it's exactly the kind of small infrastructure layer that materially improves coding-agent cost and usability.

items.title: @dkundel: A Better Way to Operate Codex in Parallel
items.body: Dkundel's tip is simple but genuinely useful: open multiple Codex windows in parallel, use /side for temporary forks, and bind a hotkey to launch new tasks quickly. It's a good reminder that a lot of agent leverage still comes from operator ergonomics, not just better underlying models.

items.title: @jakevin7: Feishu/Lark Starts Looking Like an Agent Workspace
items.body: This setup wires agents into Feishu/Lark documents, tasks, calendars, and lark-cli so work can be handed off, observed, interrupted, and corrected in place. The broader signal is that collaboration suites are becoming operational surfaces for agent teams rather than passive systems of record.

items.title: @freeportmarkets: Anthropic Secondary Prices May Have Overreacted
items.body: Freeport argues the market interpreted Anthropic's notice as if downstream secondary buyers are automatically wiped out, while Delaware precedent suggests the legal path is more nuanced. Whether or not you buy the trade, the important takeaway is that private AI valuations are now highly sensitive to legal plumbing, not just model headlines.

items.title: @servasyy_ai: Baseten Sees a Custom-Model Economy Taking Over
items.body: Summarizing Baseten's CEO, this thread claims 95% of inference tokens are now running on customized models rather than raw open-source weights. That's a meaningful market signal that value is shifting toward post-training, inference control, and proprietary workflow data instead of base-model branding alone.

items.title: @p4sc4lh: Europe Backs Harder Bargaining Rules for Platforms
items.body: The CJEU upheld Italy's position that platforms like Meta can be pushed into meaningful negotiation with press publishers and cannot rely on opacity or throttling as leverage. It's a concrete regulatory datapoint for anyone tracking how Europe intends to price platform power and content distribution.

items.title: @IntCyberDigest: The TanStack npm Compromise Was the Real Red Alert
items.body: The standout security story in the batch: compromised TanStack packages allegedly included a watcher that wipes a machine after a stolen GitHub token is revoked. More unsettling than the malware itself is the claim that the poisoned packages appeared to carry legitimate provenance, which hits directly at a core software-supply-chain trust assumption.

items.title: @DaveJ: Have Claude Output App Maps as HTML Plus JSON
items.body: Dave J's suggestion is to generate both a human-readable single-page flow document and a parallel JSON representation of the app. That's a strong pattern because it gives people something easy to review while leaving future agents a structured artifact they can reliably reuse.

items.title: @obsdmd: Obsidian Refreshes Its Community and Dev Surface
items.body: Obsidian launched a new Community site, developer dashboard, and roadmap for plugins and themes. It's not flashy, but it is a solid ecosystem update for anyone whose research or knowledge workflow depends on a healthy plugin layer.
